loquatur lingua mea in faucibus meis.
let my tongue speak along with my throat.
My words are from my simple heart,
et sententiam puram labia mea loquentur.
and my lips will speak a pure judgment.
The Spirit of God made me,
and the breath of the Almighty gave me life.

et me sicut et te fecit Deus,
God has made me, just as he also has made you,
et de eodem luto ego quoque formatus sum.
and I, likewise, have been formed of the same clay.

So, truly, do not let my wonders terrify you,
et eloquentia mea non sit tibi gravis.
and do not let my eloquence be burdensome to you.

and I have heard the voice of your words, saying:
et non est iniquitas in me.
and there is no iniquity in me.
Yet he has discovered blame in me,
ideo arbitratus est me inimicum sibi.
and so he has treated me like his enemy.
He has put my feet in fetters;
he has kept watch over all my ways.”
Hoc est ergo in quo non es justificatus:
it is for this reason that you have not been justified.
For I tell you that God is greater than man.
Adversus eum contendis, quod non ad omnia verba responderit tibi?
Do you contend against him because he has not responded to all of your words?
and he does not repeat the same thing a second time.
Through a dream in a vision of the night,
quando irruit sopor super homines, et dormiunt in lectulo,
when a deep sleep falls over men, and they are sleeping in their beds,
then, he opens the ears of men,
and, educating them, he teaches discipline,
ut avertat hominem ab his quæ facit,
so that he may divert a man from the things that he is doing,
and may free him from pride,
et vitam illius ut non transeat in gladium.

Increpat quoque per dolorem in lectulo,
Likewise, he rebukes by sorrow in bed,
et omnia ossa ejus marcescere facit.
and he causes all of his bones to become weak.
Abominabilis ei fit in vita sua panis,
Bread becomes abominable to him in his life,
et animæ illius cibus ante desiderabilis.
and, to his soul, the meat which before he desired.
and his life has drawn near to what is deadly.
Si fuerit pro eo angelus loquens,
If there were an angel speaking for him,
to declare the fairness of the man,
he will have mercy on him,
so that he will not descend to destruction.
I have found a reason to be favorable to him.
Consumpta est caro ejus a suppliciis:
His body is consumed by suffering.

and he will be soothing to him;
et videbit faciem ejus in jubilo,
and he will look upon his face in jubilation,
and he will restore his justice to man.
“I have sinned and truly I have offended,
et ut eram dignus, non recepi.
yet I was not treated as I deserved.”
Liberavit animam suam, ne pergeret in interitum,
He has freed his soul from continuing into destruction, so that,
in living, it may see the light.

Behold, all these things God works three times within each one,
ut revocet animas eorum a corruptione,
so that he may revive their souls from corruption
